_doc: Battery Ventures' cross-investor rulings for COLLECTION.md invariant 10 (run.py verify), scoped to this investor and merged at read time with data/collection/cross-investor.json. Written during the PRO-97 S2A pass, 2026-09-17; the shared file is touched only at wave alignment. `distinct` = the loose name key matched two different companies; `accepted` = the same company with a real, explained disagreement; `same` = confirmed identity. Six of the eight disagreements this pass raised were the same company and were fixed by aligning the stale side with a citation (chai-discovery, function-health and unify on Battery's side; kustomer, gogobot and motherduck on Redpoint's), which is invariant 10 working as intended.

distinct.note: different companies: Battery's 'Guild Technologies' is a compliance-list-only, exited and unresolved name, while Redpoint's 'Guild' is Guild Education, the private Denver education-benefits company whose June 2022 Series F priced it at $4.4B - Battery's own classification note already says the row is not the Denver company.

different companies: Battery's 'Northstar Technology, Inc.' is a compliance-list-only name marked exited and unrecognized, while Benchmark's 'Northstar' is a pre-window row from its 2004-2008 captures that Benchmark itself records as not resolving to any specific operating entity; only the loose name key joins them.

Different companies (PRO-136): Battery's Amplitude is the public product-analytics company (Nasdaq: AMPL). Menlo's AMPLITUDE SOFTWARE is the 1998 internet resource-scheduling company Critical Path acquired in 1999, and Menlo's own note already says it is not AMPL.

Different companies (PRO-136): Battery's Check Technologies is the New York embedded-payroll company first listed in 2023. Menlo's Check is Pageonce renamed, the mobile bill-payment app Intuit bought in 2014.

Different companies twenty-five years apart (PRO-136): Battery's Inventa Corporation is the e-business integration services firm on its 1997 portfolio page, absorbed around 2001. a16z's Inventa is the LatAm wholesale marketplace whose 2022 Series A it led.

Different companies (PRO-136): Battery's Sprig, Inc. is the 2016 compliance-list entry that fits the on-demand meal-delivery company which shut in 2017. a16z's Sprig is UserLeap renamed, the in-product research company - a16z's own note says as much.

Different companies (PRO-136): Battery's Cruise Technologies is pen-tablet computing from its 1997 portfolio page, wound down in the late 1990s. Felicis's Cruise is the self-driving company. The same pair is already ruled distinct against Spark's Cruise row.
Different companies (PRO-136): Battery's own company page locates its Jump in Salt Lake City. Menlo's JUMP is JUMP Bikes, the dockless e-bike company Uber bought in 2018 and passed to Lime in 2020.

Different companies (PRO-136): a16z's row is Forte Labs, Inc., the blockchain-gaming platform whose 2021 rounds it joined at a $1B valuation. Battery's Forte is a separate position of an earlier era on its own page; whatever it is, it is not the company a16z's $1B mark belongs to, which is what matters for the track record.
